- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is low, raise forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 10–15% in next period.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true values by >5% over 3–5 periods, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per period until convergence.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3) and forecast is volatile, smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values to reduce noise.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of historical mean, adjust downward bias by 3–5% per period.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4 → +0.6), model may be lagging — add 1–2% lag correction to forecast.
